findings.title: Exported getUser returns Promise<any>
findings.explanation: getUser is exported with return type Promise<any>, so every caller receives an unchecked value. It returns res.json() without validating the shape, and it never checks res.ok, so an error response body (for example a 404) is also typed as a User. A consumer that reads .email fails at runtime with no compile-time signal. tsconfig.json has strict: true, but explicit any is still accepted.
findings.evidence: export async function getUser(id: string): Promise<any> {
findings.suggested_fix: Declare the return type as Promise<User> (or unknown) and validate the response with a schema or type guard before returning it. Check res.ok and throw on failure before calling res.json().

findings.title: localStorage value cast straight to User
findings.explanation: localStorage.getItem returns null when the key is absent. JSON.parse(null) returns null without throwing, so loadSettings resolves to null typed as User, and a caller reading settings.email throws a TypeError. Malformed stored JSON throws a SyntaxError from the same expression. The raw as string assertion and the double cast as unknown as User hide both cases from the compiler. Assumes callers read properties of the result.
findings.evidence: return JSON.parse(raw as string) as unknown as User;
findings.suggested_fix: Handle the null case explicitly (return null or throw). Wrap JSON.parse in try/catch. Validate the parsed value with a type guard or schema, then return User | null or a narrowed User instead of casting.

findings.title: Non-null assertion on Map.get result in firstAdmin
findings.explanation: Map.get returns undefined when the key "admin" is absent. The non-null assertion removes the check, so firstAdmin throws a TypeError (Cannot read properties of undefined) when the map has no admin entry. Rated low because the origin of the map is not visible in this project; raise to medium if the users map is built from API or user input.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the result of users.get("admin") and return undefined or throw an explicit error when it is missing, e.g. const admin = users.get("admin"); if (!admin) throw new Error(...); return admin.email;
